topic_note: Gaming commentary (outside money/psychology niche). Inspired by the topic of Runtime Caffeine's Short 'The GTA 6 Situation' (https://youtube.com/shorts/KT82sgkubHU). Facts re-verified independently; wording is ours. No sourced money/psychology angle exists, so it stays pure gaming.
hook: Tomorrow, GTA six comes out. Its famous writer did not write it.
angle: Withhold WHO the writer is and WHY it matters, using a restaurant parable (famous chef quits, sign stays) that makes the viewer ask 'how can GTA 6 not be a GTA game?'. Plain facts first, then the A/B question.

claims.claim: GTA 6 releases Nov 19, 2026 (delayed from May 26, 2026), PS5 and Xbox Series X|S; Rockstar/Take-Two confirmed the date.
claims.note: Date confirmed by several outlets (TechRadar, GameLuster, PC Gamer); fetched page bodies were truncated, so the exact day comes from search summaries of those outlets.

claims.claim: Dan Houser is a Rockstar co-founder and was VP of Creative, lead writer of the GTA and Red Dead stories.
Take-Two's filing (reported Feb 4, 2020) said Houser would leave Rockstar; his last day was March 11, 2020. It said he had been on an extended break since spring 2019.
claims.note: Game Informer confirms last day March 11, 2020 and break from spring 2019; no reason was given in that article.

claims.claim: Video's claim: after RDR2 (2018) he took a vacation and never returned.
claims.note: Sources say an 'extended break' that began spring 2019 (after RDR2's Oct 2018 release). No source I opened says 'vacation'. Script says only 'a long break' and does not say 2018.

claims.claim: Video's claim: severe burnout from 100-hour work weeks caused him to leave.
claims.note: Houser said in Oct 2018 (Vulture) the team worked '100-hour weeks' on RDR2, then told Kotaku he meant only the 4-person senior writing team for about 3 weeks. His own stated reason for leaving (BBC Radio 4, reported late Nov 2025 by GamesRadar): the games were long and tough, 'I don't know if I had another one of those games in me.' No source ties his exit to 100-hour weeks, and neither he nor Rockstar is quoted saying burnout. DROPPED.

claims.claim: Houser said GTA 6 is 'not going to be a story that I wrote or a character set that I developed' (IGN interview at LA Comic Con, reported Sept 30, 2025).
claims.note: Also https://www.pcgamer.com/games/grand-theft-auto/rockstar-co-founder-dan-houser-says-he-didnt-write-any-of-gta-6-the-worlds-probably-had-enough-gta-from-me . He also said the game will be great; the script does not smear the game.

claims.claim: Houser, same IGN interview (reported Sept 30, 2025), on GTA 6: "The game will be great, I'm sure." (verbatim quote)
claims.note: Verbatim wording as quoted by TechRadar (script QA v5 confirmed on the page). Used in line 6: 'He also said GTA six will be great.'

claims.claim: Video's claim: in 2022 Rockstar encouraged writers not to offend anyone.
claims.note: No 2022 primary report found. What exists: Bloomberg (Jason Schreier, Dec 2024) reported Rockstar asked GTA 6 writers to be 'less crude' toward transgender people and other minorities; no Rockstar comment found. Different year and narrower than 'not offend anyone'. DROPPED.

reveal: The famous writer behind GTA's stories is Dan Houser, and he said he wrote none of GTA 6.
open_loop: Line 1 withholds who the writer is; lines 2-3 (restaurant parable) tease the problem; the name is revealed in line 4; the GTA question is paid in the last line.
payoff: Plain facts: Houser wrote Rockstar's famous stories, left in March 2020 after a long break, and said he wrote none of GTA 6. Then: still a GTA game?
ab_idea: A: Still a GTA game. B: Not a GTA game. Splits fans (name/world/studio vs the writer). Alternative test: 'A: The name is enough / B: The writer was the heart'.
notes_for_scriptwriter: Phrase everything as 'he said' / reported. No Rockstar logos, art, footage, music or characters; 'GTA 6' plain text only. Do not claim burnout, vacation, 2018, 100-hour weeks or the 2022 offend claim. Do not say the game is bad.
